Author: deserokk
Name: DeserokUtils
Description:
Small quality-of-life utilities, one feature per tab.

CastWatch: gate a macro line on whether an action actually went off. Arm a watch above the /ac, then /ifwatch runs your line only if the action was accepted -- or cancels the macro if it was not. Works for instant casts, oGCDs and usable items, none of which produce a cast bar to observe. Optional target filters (--self, --notself, --party) and a {who} token that fills in whoever actually received it, which a vanilla macro cannot do.

FateWatch: warn before a cyclic FATE spawns. Built for Occult Crescent's pot FATEs, which run on a rotation the game surfaces nowhere. Server-bar countdown plus toast and sound alerts, predicted from the last spawn it actually saw -- and it says 'not seen yet' rather than inventing a number.

FcBuffs: keep the Free Company buffs running. Checks whether the buffs you picked are still up and refreshes them from the FC's existing stock, in cities and residential districts only. It spends no credits: activating an action the FC already bought is free. Tells you when one runs out somewhere it cannot refresh, and when the stock is gone. A dry-run mode is available that rehearses every step and logs what it would have done, without activating anything.

DrawSheathe: one key that draws or sheathes, whichever is currently correct. The Gold Saucer draw and sheathe animations are separate emotes rather than replacements for the default weapon toggle, so they cannot be bound as a toggle and take two hotbar slots. /drawsheathe reads whether your weapon is out and plays the right one. The emote is silently refused while you are moving or jumping, so those fall back to the game's own draw/sheathe and a single key covers every case. Both emote commands are configurable, and a held key collapses to one toggle.

EmoteQuiet: announce an emote the first time, then stay quiet about repeats of that same emote for a minute. Clapping through a whole performance says you clapped once instead of fifty times. The game only offers all-or-nothing, which is why most people switch emote log messages off entirely and then nobody ever knows they clapped at all. Optionally hides other people's repeats from your own log too -- kept per sender, so ten people clapping is still ten lines and one person clapping thirty times is one.

Mouseover: /ifmo picks the first target the action would actually land on. Write {mo}, or chain candidates like {mo|2}, ending with |noop to send nothing at all when none of them would land. One line replaces the twelve-line mouseover macro with a fallback at the bottom, and removes the race where pressing early lands the fallback instead of the mouseover.

Interact: /dsuinteract operates the thing in front of you and nothing else. FFXIV's Confirm key is console-shaped -- it drives world objects AND menus, and takes two presses for a lever, so you press it repeatedly. With a menu open those presses land in the menu and activate whatever is under the cursor. A dedicated key cannot do that, because it is not Confirm. It also never changes your target, so you are not left pointed at a lever afterwards.

Everything here happens because you pressed something. The one exception is FcBuffs, which you switch on deliberately.
